artifacts.title: Biese et al. v. Tennessee Valley Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: Tennessee Valley Presbytery approved without exception Session minutes planning a youth group Super Bowl Party on Sunday; the SJC denied the complaint because the record was insufficient to find Presbytery erred in its constitutional interpretation. A dissent by RE Eggert argued the complaint was judicially out of order because the SJC lacks constitutional authority to review a presbytery's session-records review decisions under BCO 40-2 and 40-3.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Huffman filed an appeal after the 50th GA amended BCO 38-1 to change the remedy from complaint to appeal, but his case originated and was nearly complete under the prior rule allowing complaint. The SJC found the case judicially out of order and remanded to Tennessee Valley Presbytery to adjudicate as a complaint under the then-existing rule, resetting the clock for presbytery action.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Knox Baird and other elders challenged Grace Presbytery's handling of complaints, BCO 40-5 review requests, document demands, and a stay of pending trials arising from conflict at First Presbyterian Church of Hattiesburg. The SJC sustained the complaints in the main, rejected one specification, and did not reach another; concurring opinions were recorded.

artifacts.synopsis: TE Aaron Myers appealed his conviction on charges of maltreatment of his wife and fits of anger by Illiana Presbytery; the SJC denied the appeal and upheld all four specifications of error arguments raised by the appellant, affirming the indefinite suspension from office and suspension from the sacraments.
